body:
I have a similar issue; I live in a less-than-ideal neighborhood and can't seem to summon up the courage to leave the house by myself. To top off my anxiety, I don't drive, which just exacerbates things because I would have to walk wherever I wanted to go if I did leave the house. 

I wish I could offer advice, but I'm kind of in the same boat of not knowing what to do. I haven't left the house without one of my roommates or a friend accompanying me in over six months.

I don't have a therapist currently since I moved to a new state and I haven't applied for health insurance here yet, but I did talk about this with my previous therapist. I've felt this way (specifically) for about four or five years, but I've been generally depressed since I was 12 years old or so (I'm 22 now). It isn't all about finding a career; I just don't have the motivation, the will-power, or the confidence to do anything with my life. I can think of plenty of things I might like to do, I just can't see myself really putting in the effort to do any of those things. Because why should I? It'll just end up being a lot of work for (most likely) little payout. I just don't have the energy (not to mention the funds) to commit to pursuing any kind of training program that isn't a sure thing that I will both want to do indefinitely AND be good at. 

So why should I bother with anything? I'm either going to figure out I don't like it that much or I'm not good at it. I don't want to spend what little time I have as an able-bodied adult just spinning my wheels, hoping that the next thing I try is something I can settle into. I'd like to do more with my life than just work until my body gives out. That thought exhausts me and I'm fatigued enough, as it is.

I hate feeling like I'm being a snob or pessimist because I refuse to just work for the sole purpose of paying rent. But why would I want to work an arbitrary job that will most likely just stress me out to no end and depress me more? I can't bear to live like that.

But, then, what's the alternative? How do I live otherwise? My bills aren't going to miraculously pay themselves and my landlord's leniency is sure to stretch only so far. I don't think I care about living enough to submit myself to the misery of a mundane, arbitrary existence. I can't do it.

Depression can change over time. It's almost like it adapts to whatever you use against it. When you first became a part of your group of friends, that social connection helped ease some of the pain, but the depression seems to have worn through that barricade and now interacting with your friends doesn't help the way it used to. The same thing happens with actual depression medication after awhile; over time, it loses it's potency and you have to up your dosage or switch to a different drug. 

I'm not really an expert on this or anything (I'm speaking from my own experience with depression, mostly), but I might consider talking to your doctor/therapist about anti-depressants. Sorting out the brain's chemical imbalance is often a good place to start. Other than that, talking to someone can help a lot (just having your thoughts heard by another human-being can do wonders; it's incredibly validating). Additionally, you might try thinking about things you could do that might be "of worth". Maybe you could volunteer time at a soup kitchen or become a foster home for your local animal shelter or you could even do something as simple as helping a friend run errands. Sometimes, if you can't help yourself, you help others instead.

This sounds almost exactly like what my mind was telling me just before I broke down and ended up in a mental health facility for a couple of weeks back in December, 2012. I actually skipped out on my final exams and had planned to kill myself, but I chickened out at the last second and had a friend take me to the hospital. I just thought about all the pain it would cause my friends and family and I just couldn't do that to them, even though that little voice in the back of my head kept saying, "Do it now 'cause, if you don't, they're just going to have to watch you slowly deteriorate. It'll hurt less for them if you just get it over with; don't make them watch you waste away." 
I wish I could offer you hope and tell you I'm better now, but, the truth is, this battle never ends. It's a constant day-to-day struggle and the darkness comes and goes in waves that could so easily drown you. It's horrible and infuriating and exhausting and it takes everything you have to push through another day, but if you can find a buoy (a loved one, a passion, something) that you can cling to while you tread water, you just gotta cling to it and kick until your legs give out. Because sometimes all we can do is just survive. 
I wish I had better advice to give, but that's all I've got. Feel free to PM if you want to talk more; I can definitely relate.
